newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Gov. building plans may strain budget - report.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Gov. building plans may strain budget - report.

text.p: Mass. Gov. William Weld's pledge to build convention centers, sports areanas and other projects may strain the state's budget, the Boston Globe reported Tuesday.

The governor and the state Legislature have agreed to limit state infrastructure spending to $900 million a year, but they have authorized $8.8 billion in infrastrucutre projects, from the Central Artery Project or "Big Dig" to a new Boston courthouse, the newspaper said. Weld, who labelled himself Gov. Pothole recently because of his enthusiasm for building projects, also wants to remove tollbooths from the Massachusetts Turnpike, putting further pressure on the budget.
"Gov. Pothole? Sounds more like Gov. Pothead," House Speaker Thomas Finneran said. "We do not have unlimited funds."
The state's infrastructure spending is financed by debt, and over the last year, while Weld was running unsuccessfully for the U.S. Senate, he signed a slew of bond bills.

In February, he authorized $486 million to build prisons, $399 million to buy environmentally sensitive land and $280 million to revitalize seaports, the Globe reported. He later approved $2.1 bilion for transportation, $736 million for state, college and other public buildings and $394 million for computers, the newspaper said.
"There's such a long list of projects waiting for money, the pressure is just incredible," Michael Widmer, director of the Massachusetts Taypayers Foundation told the Globe.
